analysis.body:
The Census BTOS series reports construction AI use directly from firms on a fortnightly basis. For Construction (NAICS 23), the latest reading is 16.0% of firms answering yes to using AI in the last two weeks, compared with 14.3% in the prior period. The series first asked the question in September 2023.

Per AGC, BuiltWorlds, and the proptech and contech trackers, construction AI deployments include computer-vision safety monitoring, BIM clash detection, and autonomous site scanning. BuiltWorlds runs an annual AI/ML Conference that covers existing and emerging solutions and use cases across the construction, building, and operation process, along with strategies for project and enterprise level implementation and case studies showing lessons learned.

Vendor and capital activity concentrates in industry networks and events. BuiltWorlds' annual Buildings Conference examines data centers and AI infrastructure, while its AI/ML Conference showcases founders and practical AI applications in construction. CREtech New York 2026, described as the world's premier real estate AI conference, expects 3,000 leaders, 150 speakers, and 20,000+ 1:1 meetings on October 20, 21, 2026 at the Javits Center, NYC, with sessions led by operators actively deploying AI and sponsors representing companies shaping real estate in the age of AI. CREtech and MetaProp track venture flow across architecture, engineering, and construction technology alongside property tech.

The excerpts do not report quantified return on investment for construction AI. BuiltWorlds points to case studies and lessons learned, and CREtech promises real strategy from CIOs, CEOs, and MDs moving real assets with real AI, but neither provides ROI figures. AGC's excerpt covers construction input costs climbing 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026, contractors adding 22,000 jobs in August, a construction unemployment rate of 3.1%, and firms struggling to fill openings, which is labor and cost context rather than AI performance data.

The source excerpts are silent on AI-specific risks and regulatory posture. AGC mentions safety-technology compliance, but no regulatory detail on AI appears in these pages. A reader deciding whether to deploy should weigh the measured 16.0% adoption, the concrete use cases, and the active vendor and capital networks against the absence of published ROI and regulatory guidance in these sources, and seek operator case studies from BuiltWorlds and CREtech events before committing.

https://cretech.com/.brief: According to the page, CREtech New York 2026 will be held at the Javits Center in New York City on October 20, 21, 2026, and will bring together 3,000 leaders, 150 speakers, and more than 20,000 pre-scheduled 1:1 meetings. The event is described as a leading real-estate AI conference where sessions are led by operators actively deploying AI in their portfolios, offering real strategy rather than theory. The conference aims to connect owners, developers, investors, occupiers, construction firms, brokers, and tech leaders to discuss AI’s impact on real-estate assets. Tickets are limited, and sponsors and partners are said to represent companies shaping the future of real-estate in the age of AI.

https://www.agc.org/.brief: The Associated General Contractors of America describes offerings for its more than 27,000 member firms, including a safety conference in San Diego and a course for project executives. The association reports that construction input costs rose 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026, and its survey found war and tariff effects are disrupting projects. It also states contractors added 22,000 jobs in August, with the construction unemployment rate hitting a record low of 3.1%, while firms struggle to fill open positions.

https://builtworlds.com/.brief: BuiltWorlds operates a membership network for buildings and infrastructure professionals. The organization hosts an annual Buildings Conference addressing innovation in building development, design, materials and systems, with particular focus on data centers and AI infrastructure. It also runs an annual AI/ML Conference exploring artificial intelligence and machine learning adoption across the architecture, engineering, construction and operations industry, covering implementation strategies, use cases, and lessons learned from companies deploying these technologies.
